meta_title: Sublime Text Alternative for Mac: jplus2 Compared
meta_description: Sublime Text alternative for Mac? Compare jplus2, a native Mac editor with a free Lite version, with Sublime Text's strengths and trade-offs.
h1: Sublime Text alternative for Mac: jplus2 compared
lead: Sublime Text is fast, mature and extensible, and it runs on Windows, Mac and Linux. jplus2 is Mac-only and takes a different route: a native editor with run, debug, SQL, GitHub and AI built in. This comparison uses Sublime's own pages and says where each one is stronger.
card_text: Sublime Text's strengths and trade-offs next to jplus2, a Mac-only editor with a free Lite version.

sections.h2: What Sublime Text says about itself
sections.html:
From sublimetext.com and its store page, checked in November 2026:

  • It runs on Windows, Mac and Linux, with Apple silicon support.
  • It highlights GPU rendering and lower memory use.
  • It offers Goto Anything, multiple selections and split editing.
  • It has a Python 3.8 plugin API and a package ecosystem.
  • Personal licenses are a once-off purchase with 3 years of updates, and it can be evaluated for free.

Sublime Textjplus2
PlatformsWindows, Mac and LinuxmacOS only, with an iPadOS version planned
CostPaid license (once-off, 3 years of updates), free evaluationLite is free; the full version is on the Mac App Store
Extending itPython API and packagesNo plugin system: features are built in
Built inEditor features; extend with packagesFull version: run, debug, SQL, GitHub and an AI assistant
MaturityLong establishedVersion 1.0, one author
SpeedGPU rendering, according to the vendorNot benchmarked: we publish no speed claims

• You work on more than one operating system.
  • You want plugins, packages or a Python API.
  • You value years of polish and a large ecosystem.

• You work on a Mac and want a native Cocoa editor.
  • You want run, debug, SQL, GitHub and AI without installing packages (full version).
  • You want no account and no telemetry, and a free Lite to start with.

• Built-in IntelliSense covers C, C++, Objective-C, Swift and Python; other languages use a language server only if one is installed on your Mac, otherwise keywords and words from the file.
  • There is no plugin ecosystem.
  • It is version 1.0, so it is less proven on huge files and unusual workflows.

faq.a: It can be downloaded and evaluated for free, but continued use needs a license, according to sublimehq.com.
Yes. It is a free download of about {size}, with no account.
For editing on a Mac, often yes. If you rely on Sublime's packages or on cross-platform work, no.
